story: Change of use is taking a bigger share of padel growth: 29% of new-court submissions were change of use, and the former Homebase on Finchley Road reached 10 courts.
hold_back: See all 47 approvals of five courts or more from the last twelve months, with addresses, decision dates, court counts and former building type in Padel Genie.
why_it_works: It gives one clear structural shift, proves it with a named scheme people will remember, and holds back the actionable list inside Padel Genie.
improve: It would be better with one more named reuse example tied to the same shift in the main creative, such as Merlin Way or Trident Trade Park.

story: July was revised from 63 lodged applications to 93 as reported in August, a reminder that council planning data arrives late rather than all at once.
hold_back: Use Padel Genie’s daily-updated planning application map to track new applications as councils publish.
why_it_works: It turns a dry caveat into a useful industry point about how planning data behaves, backed by a clean before-and-after number.
improve: It would be better with a named council example showing the lag in practice, if a verified atom for one is available.

story: Covered and indoor schemes are larger on average: 3.18 courts versus 2.51 outdoors, with the former Homebase on Finchley Road a 10-court example.
hold_back: Open the list of 47 approvals of five courts or more to inspect bigger covered schemes and former building types.
why_it_works: It is a clean like-for-like comparison with a memorable named example, without over-claiming what size differences mean.
improve: It would be better with a verified named outdoor comparator so both sides of the comparison carry a place, not just the covered side.

story: Carbon Padel Club and Rocks Lane Chiswick were the highest revenue-generating padel clubs in the country in August, according to the August report.
hold_back: Club X-Ray shows every bookable club in the country with occupancy, price and estimated revenue.
why_it_works: It broadens the batch beyond planning and gives operators a named benchmark while keeping the underlying club-by-club detail inside the product.
improve: It would be better with a verified hero number for either club’s revenue or occupancy, since the current story relies on rank without a numeric lead.
